subject: English
passage: In bioluminescent signaling, specialized cells called photophores emit coordinated flashes of light so bright that they can be seen across vast ocean distances. Until recently, this phenomenon has only been observed in deep-sea environments because photophores cannot coordinate effectively under high atmospheric pressure. But in a study, Dr. Nyala Kiros and colleagues observed bioluminescent signaling in shallow-water organisms using modified algae and other pressure-sensitive organisms; the researchers propose that the formation of pressure-regulating vesicles called barosomes in the organisms shields photophores from atmospheric interference.
prompt: Based on the text, how are barosomes believed to be involved in the bioluminescent signaling observed in Kiros and colleagues' study?

choices.A: Barosomes enable bioluminescent signals to transfer from one pressure-sensitive organism to another.
choices.B: Barosomes allow for the photophores to coordinate despite higher atmospheric pressure.
choices.C: Barosomes accelerate the photophores' release of bioluminescent flashes.
choices.D: Barosomes reduce the brightness of the bioluminescent signals.

explanation:
Choice B is the best answer because it most accurately describes Kiros and colleagues' claim about how the barosomes function in relation to bioluminescent signaling. The text indicates that 'until recently,' bioluminescent signaling (bright, coordinated flashes of light emitted by photophores) has solely been observed in deep-sea environments. However, it also states that, recently, Kiros and colleagues report observing the phenomenon in shallow water. They achieved this using 'modified algae and other pressure-sensitive organisms,' which the researchers claim allows for the formation of barosomes. They also suggest that these barosomes might shield against the atmospheric pressure that typically disrupts photophore coordination in shallow water. Thus, based on the text, Kiros and colleagues believe that barosomes help photophores coordinate under pressure conditions well above those at which bioluminescent signaling had previously been observed.

Why A is incorrect:

Choice A is incorrect because the text doesn't address the prospect of a bioluminescent signal moving between pressure-sensitive organisms or any other mediums.
